summary: Grey cement, ready-mix concrete, white cement and related materials used to build and finish homes and other structures.
description: UltraTech makes cement and other building materials and sells them through shops and directly to business customers. For example, a homebuilder may buy cement bags, while a contractor may order a truck of prepared concrete. The company must make the material and get it to the right place in usable condition.
money: Customers pay for cement, concrete and related products. The company pays for stone and other ingredients, fuel, electricity, workers, factories and transport. It must also maintain equipment and fund expansion. The selling price of a tonne is not the profit left from it.
customers: Dealers supplying homebuilders, contractors, property developers and customers building roads, factories or other large projects.
drivers: How much construction is happening nearby, local selling prices, fuel and electricity bills, transport distance and how much of the factory’s available production customers actually buy.

groups.title: Grey cement
groups.examples: UltraTech cement ranges for buildings and infrastructure.
groups.explanation: Cement is a binding ingredient. Builders combine it with water and other materials to make concrete; cement and concrete are not the same product.

groups.title: Ready-mix concrete
groups.examples: Concrete prepared to an agreed requirement and sent to a site.
groups.explanation: The contractor buys prepared concrete rather than mixing all its ingredients on site. It must arrive at the right time and meet the agreed requirements; it cannot sit in a shop like a sealed cement bag.

groups.title: White cement and wall-finishing products
groups.examples: Birla White cement, wall putty and related finishes.
groups.explanation: These help with appearance and surface finishing. Wall putty smooths a surface before decoration. Those uses differ from the main structural uses of grey cement.

groups.title: Other building products and support
groups.examples: Ultravolt electrical wires and cables, launched in July–September 2026, plus other construction products and building-support offerings.
groups.explanation: Wires and cables carry electricity through a building. They are made mainly from copper and aluminium and sold through retailers to electricians and other buyers, so their materials and customers differ from cement’s. A product name helps identify what the customer buys. It does not mean the company separately reports that product’s profit; UltraTech reports all its building materials as one business.

basics.title: How does stone become cement?
basics.text: The process prepares raw materials, heats them to make an intermediate material called clinker, then grinds and blends it into cement. A grinding unit handles a later step; a plant that also makes clinker needs different equipment and costs.

steps.title: Obtain ingredients and permissions
steps.text: Arrange limestone and other materials, fuel and electricity, with the permissions required to operate.

steps.title: Make and check the material
steps.text: Use heating and grinding equipment to produce cement that meets its stated requirements, or prepare the ordered concrete.

steps.title: Send it to the shop or construction site
steps.text: Move bags or bulk loads to buyers. Longer journeys and delivery delays can make each sale more costly.

steps.title: Collect payment and keep the plant running
steps.text: Customer payments must cover production, transport, repairs, borrowing and other costs. New factories need further investment before they earn from sales.

specifics.title: A nearby market matters more than a national headline
specifics.text: Cement prices depend partly on local building work, competing suppliers and delivery distance. Construction growth somewhere else does not guarantee better prices near each factory.

specifics.title: The factory’s size is different from actual sales
specifics.text: Capacity is how much a plant could produce under stated conditions. Actual production and sales may be lower while demand builds or equipment is stopped. Utilisation means how much of that capacity is being used.

specifics.title: Read the cost of getting each tonne to a buyer
specifics.text: Fuel, electricity, ingredients and transport can change separately. More tonnes sold can leave little extra profit if the cost of making and moving them also rises.

watch: Can the company sell at useful prices in its local markets?
Nearby competitors and building activity affect prices.
Read local demand, selling-price and quantity commentary together. A national construction headline does not describe every factory’s market.
What remains after making and moving each tonne?
Fuel and transport bills can rise even while sales grow.
Read the company’s per-tonne cost and earnings measures and their definitions. Compare fuel, power, materials and transport over matching periods.
Are new factories producing goods that customers buy?
Announced capacity is not the same as sales.
Check when equipment starts, how much it produces and what is sold. Buying an existing competitor adds capacity to UltraTech but does not itself add new factories to the industry.
Factories and acquisitions can consume cash before earning it back.
Read cash generated by day-to-day operations, then spending on equipment and acquisitions. Also check unsold stock and customer payments still outstanding.
Are permissions, safety and acquired operations being managed?
A stopped quarry or plant can interrupt supply.
Read mining, environmental, safety and acquisition disclosures. Separate an announcement from an approved, finished plant that has begun commercial production.
risks: Producers may lower prices to win buyers even when more cement is being used.
Coal, other fuels, electricity and moving materials can raise the cost of each sale.
Expansion takes too long to earn back its cost
New or acquired factories need money, maintenance and enough buyers.
Permit problems, lost quarry access, accidents or equipment failures can stop work and add costs.
context: New factory capacity and a new product in the September 2026 quarter

UltraTech’s 19 October 2026 results release says that in July–September 2026 it started a new cement plant at Petnikota, Andhra Pradesh, and squeezed extra output from three existing plants. It also says it sold more grey cement in India than a year earlier and used a larger share of its factories’ capacity. Capacity utilisation means how much of the possible production was actually used. Sales and profit both rose. In the same quarter it launched Ultravolt wires and cables, made at a newly started factory in Jhagadia, Gujarat. A new factory or product begins with spending; whether it earns depends on buyers ordering enough over the following years.
quiz: Does buying more cement factories guarantee more profit?
No. Demand, selling prices, actual factory use, fuel, transport and the purchase price of those factories all matter.
sources: Results for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, new capacity and Ultravolt launch · 19 October 2026

financialNotes.title: Match tonnes, periods and the profit measure
financialNotes.text: The table uses audited consolidated revenue from operations and statutory group profit after tax, including exceptional items. It does not substitute a net-sales or adjusted-profit press-release headline. Match the reporting period with volume disclosures; capacity is not sales, and company profit is not a profit allocation to cement, concrete or individual brands.
